sections.h2: Which Kalamazoo offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
Two city offices split the work. The Assessor sets the value, and the Treasurer sends and collects the bills. The assessor sits in City Hall at 241 W South Street, with counter hours of 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, phone (269) 337-8000 and email assessor@kalamazoocity.org. Payments can also go into a drop box at the City Hall entrance at any hour, or a drive-up box on St. Johns Place at West Lovell Street.

Once the local collection window shuts, the Kalamazoo County Treasurer inherits the unpaid balance. Sellers get caught out at that handoff, because the county adds heavier charges than the city does.

Wikipedia counts 73,598 people in the 2020 census and calls Kalamazoo the county seat. Settlers arrived in 1829, the place was known as Bronson until 1836, and today it hosts Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo College and Kalamazoo Valley Community College.

sections.h2: What are the due dates for a Kalamazoo tax bill?
sections.html:
The year's tax arrives in two bills. The summer bill goes out by July 1 and is due July 31, and it can be settled at once or split into six monthly installments that carry no interest when paid on time. The winter bill goes out by December 1, is due February 14 of the next year, and must be paid in a single payment.

Kalamazoo city property tax calendar, from the city's payment page and the county foreclosure timeline
DateEvent
By July 1Summer bills mailed
July 31Summer bill or first installment due; late payers face a one time 3% charge and 1% interest each month after
By December 1Winter bills mailed
February 14Winter bill due
March 1Anything left unpaid is delinquent and goes to the County Treasurer

Card users pay the processor 2.8 percent, with a $1.50 floor, and electronic check users pay $0.85. A check dropped at City Hall carries no such add on.

sections.h2: What does it cost when a Kalamazoo bill goes delinquent?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer tacks on a 4 percent administrative fee and 1 percent interest every month, along with charges for mailings, recording, title work and site visits. The county's sample timeline for 2025 taxes runs as follows:

  • The last day to pay at the local office is February 28, and later payments go to the county.
  • A $15 notice charge lands on October 1 of the next year.
  • On the following March 1, a parcel more than a year behind is forfeited, with half a percent monthly interest, 6 percent retroactive interest and a $175 title search charge.
  • Recording certificates adds $60, an in person site visit $50, and the newspaper listing $50.
  • After 25 months unpaid, title moves to the County Treasurer on April 1.

Once the county owns the parcel, the owner cannot take it back. A person named on the deed may claim surplus money from an auction sale, and no treasurer can waive penalties or interest.

sections.h2: Is there a way to delay or spread out Kalamazoo property tax?
sections.html:
Several routes exist. A low income owner can ask to defer the summer bill until the winter due date. The prior year's household income must have been $40,000 or less, and the applicant must be 62 or older, an unmarried surviving spouse of someone who was, blind, paraplegic, hemiplegic, quadriplegic, totally and permanently disabled, or an eligible veteran, service member, widow or widower. The City Treasurer's Office takes applications through September 15, and winter bills cannot be deferred.

After a bill reaches the county, the Treasurer can sign an extension agreement at an appointment with its foreclosure prevention team, reachable at 269-384-8124. The county expects two tax years to be cleared each calendar year, and dangerous or condemned buildings are not eligible.

Partial payments to the county are welcome because they slow the monthly interest. Staff there also check eligibility for the principal residence, poverty and disabled veteran exemptions.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Kalamazoo property assessment?
sections.html:
Go first to the March Board of Review. MCL 211.30 sets its opening for the second Monday of March, with the city allowed to choose the Tuesday or Wednesday after. The board sits at least 12 hours that week, including 3 hours after 6 p.m.

When it agrees the value is off, it adjusts the assessed and taxable amounts to a fair level. You then receive written word of the outcome by the first Monday in June, with notice of the right to appeal further.

That next level is the Michigan Tax Tribunal, an independent tax court. Its Small Claims division hears most residential appeals in informal telephone sessions of about half an hour, and owners often appear without a lawyer. The board's notice gives the last day to file, so check it on arrival.

sections.h2: What certificates does a Kalamazoo house sale need?
sections.html:
A warranty deed needs two. In the city, the County Treasurer will not issue a certificate until the City Treasurer has issued one, for $10 at City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036. The county certificate then costs $5 for up to 20 tax ID numbers. The state rule is MCL 211.135, which looks back five years from the deed date.

At the recording counter, 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, the seller also owes transfer tax of $1.10 per $1,000 to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state, after rounding the price up to the next $500. Applied to the city's Census median value of $179,000, that totals $1,539.40. The deed itself costs $30 to record.

Tax owed on the house is usually paid out of closing proceeds. Ask the treasurer holding the bill for the payoff, because city and county records are updated separately.

sections.h2: Which Kalamazoo exemption matters when I sell?
sections.html:
The principal residence exemption cuts part of the local school operating tax on a home you own and live in. The city says you qualify by owning and occupying the home on May 1 and filing the affidavit with the Assessor.

A sale changes the filing. The seller files a rescission with the assessor, and the buyer files a fresh affidavit. An owner who buys a replacement home may keep the exemption on the old one for as long as three years while it stands empty, is for sale, is not rented and is not used for business. That request is due by May 1 after the new home claims the exemption, and it is refiled by December 31 each year to continue for up to two more.

Tell the closing agent when you moved out. A wrong exemption status on a sold house leads to corrected bills later.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for the city of Kalamazoo?
sections.html:
Renters outnumber owners here, which is unusual for a Michigan city of this size. QuickFacts lists 72,683 residents in mid 2025 and 29,523 households, with owners in only 42.3 percent of homes.

  • Middle home value: $179,000.
  • Monthly gross rent, midpoint: $1,078.
  • Household income, midpoint: $52,272, with 24.9 percent of residents below the poverty line.
  • Land: 24.69 square miles, roughly 2,980 residents each square mile.
  • Bachelor's degree or more, adults 25 and up: 38.5 percent.

Landlords with tenants, inherited houses and homes with deferred repairs often arrive at a sale with tax balances. The city's online parcel lookup on BS&A shows tax history, payment dates and amounts due along with permit history, so look yours up before you list.

faqs.q: When is the winter property tax due in Kalamazoo?
faqs.a: It is due February 14 of the year after it is billed, and a winter bill has to be paid in full. Unpaid winter and summer bills become delinquent on March 1 and move to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I pay Kalamazoo summer taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. You can pay the summer bill in six monthly payments by paying the first installment by July 31. If the first payment is late, a one time 3 percent penalty applies and interest of 1 percent is charged on the first of each month.

faqs.q: Who sets the assessed value of a house in Kalamazoo?
faqs.a: The City Assessor's Office does. If you disagree, the March Board of Review is the first place to appeal, followed by the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

faqs.q: Who qualifies to defer Kalamazoo summer taxes?
faqs.a: Owners with household income of $40,000 or less in the prior year who are 62 or older, disabled, blind, or an eligible veteran, service member, widow or widower. Applications are due September 15 to the City Treasurer.

faqs.q: What does a Kalamazoo tax certificate cost?
faqs.a: The city certificate costs $10 and the county certificate costs $5 for up to 20 tax ID numbers. Both are needed for a warranty deed on a property inside the city.
